<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/service-settings`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via SettingsService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via SettingsService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/config-resolution.mdx`  _(via SettingsService (symbol, a top-level class), registerSettingsRoutes (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via SettingsService (symbol, a top-level class))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c0abfb7df393ec3a6cb7501191fa265581006faf` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b55a0b27d1ba827f0a5ba384dc4fd02a1d9c029f` — the merge of head `0190f5a236613dd7e360e0fc25b92339745bdfbf` into base `c0abfb7df393ec3a6cb7501191fa265581006faf`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b55a0b27d1ba827f0a5ba384dc4fd02a1d9c029f && git checkout b55a0b27d1ba827f0a5ba384dc4fd02a1d9c029f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c0abfb7df393ec3a6cb7501191fa265581006faf 0190f5a236613dd7e360e0fc25b92339745bdfbf && git checkout -B drift-repro c0abfb7df393ec3a6cb7501191fa265581006faf && git merge --no-ff 0190f5a236613dd7e360e0fc25b92339745bdfbf

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c0abfb7df393ec3a6cb7501191fa265581006faf
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c0abfb7df393ec3a6cb7501191fa265581006faf` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `047e94d64a6c6d731ae6cad147d4af312184280a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/settings-manifest.zod.ts + packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.types.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-routes.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-routes.live-status.pin.test.ts, packages/spec/src/system/settings-manifest.test.ts, packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json, content/docs/references/system/settings-manifest.mdx, docs/audits/2026-07-unknown-key-strictness-ledger.counts/system.md, .changeset/32052-settings-live-values.md

Read: PR #32057 diff against merge base `fcb2122d` (14 files, +371/-20), card #32052, the seat delta and step-0 rulings, the dev report 6759350718, the PR body, and the head's check-runs. Nothing built or run locally.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Served answers that existed before: unchanged.** `liveStatementOf` returns `{}` with no provider and with a provider answering a falsy status; a banner-only statement returns `{ banner }` built from the same six fields in the same order as `main`'s `liveStatusOf`; the throw arm keeps the same warn text and the same error banner. The route spreads `live` only when it is set, after `values`, so a page with no provider or a banner-only provider serialises the same keys in the same order. Neither in-repo provider (`plugin-email` for `mail`, `localization-currency-lock` for `localization`) states `values`, so neither starts taking the new branch. `getNamespace` returns no `live` key of its own, so the spread cannot collide.
- **Gate order: held.** The read route calls `getNamespace` first (`assertPermitted(…, 'read', ctx)` → `SettingsForbiddenError` → 403 `SETTINGS_FORBIDDEN`), then `liveStatementOf`. The family door's 401 / held-session refusals run before both. `liveStatementOf` has exactly one caller in the repo (`settings-routes.ts:316`); the aggregate `GET /api/settings` serves `listManifests` only and never asks a live-status provider; PUT and the action routes do not serve `live`. No second door.
- **No secret reaches the response.** A served entry is a fresh `{ value, source }` literal; the key must be in `reg.scopes` and have an option table (declared non-empty, or a registered source); `source` is checked against the closed three; `'none'` requires `value === null`; any other source requires a primitive string that `table.judge` admits. The error-banner arm carries no `values`, so a throw serves no `live`. `payload.values` redaction is untouched.
- **No secret reaches the new log line.** The `dropped` strings are a provider-supplied key name plus a fixed reason; the value, the entry and the source are never interpolated. (The pre-existing throw warn still prints `err.message`; unchanged by this PR.)
- **Spec against runtime.** `live` is `.optional()`, a record of `{ value: string | null, source: enum(settings, environment, none) }`, inline, no new export; every body the runtime can serve parses (pinned with `SettingsNamespacePayloadSchema.safeParse` on the served body in three pins). The schema is a superset of the runtime rule (it does not carry "null iff none"; the description states it), which is the right direction for a response schema. Regenerated artifacts present: the reference page, `authorable-surface/system.json` (one row), the `system/` strictness count (401 → 402, the one new inline object site).
- **Pins against rulings.** Invalid entry beside a valid banner (the ⛔ credential-as-value pin and eight `it.each` cases, each asserting the stated label and severity survive and one warn); valid beside invalid (`provider` served, `embedder_provider` dropped, one warn naming the key, no secret); throw → error banner and no `live`; unknown (no provider, banner-only → `'live' in body` false) vs `none` (served only as stated); extra fields `apiKey` / `keyPrefix` absent from the body; 403 with `provider` never called. Each ruling has a pin, and the dev's six ablations each turned one red.
- **Test-double renames: forced.** The three route doubles (`anonymous-floor`, `auth-gate`, `authz-outage-relay`) stubbed `liveStatusOf`; the route now calls `liveStatementOf`, so an unrenamed stub is a `TypeError` in the read handler. One line each, same meaning (`{}` = nothing to state). Step 0 named two; the third is declared in the PR body and the report. Not scope creep.
- **PR body.** Census present and accurate: `gateway`, `openai`, `anthropic`, `google` are at `ai.manifest.ts:51-54` at this head, 4 of 4. "Carried to repo:cloud" present and accurate: service-ai fills `values.provider` in its `registerLiveStatus('ai', …)` call, `settings` / `environment` / `none`, with a memory or echo fallback stated as `{ value: null, source: 'none' }` and never `memory`.

### ② Semver level

**Refused by the head's own gate.** `Check Changeset` is red on `047e94d6` (job 129638787021), verdict `none-baseline-moved`: the PR declares `Metadata-protocol: none` and moves `packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json` (the new row `system/SettingsNamespacePayload:live`). The level axis in `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` treats a moved authorable-surface shard as a key entering the metadata protocol, whatever the key is for; `none` may not move one, and the gate's own text bars editing the baseline to quiet it.

So the step-0 ruling (`Metadata-protocol: none`, both packages `patch`) cannot stand as written. Ruling A on #25105 still decides the level, but its input here is `added`, not `none`: the gate's reading is that `SettingsNamespacePayload` sits in the authorable register (`manifest` and `values` are already rows there), so a new key on it is `added` → at least one moved package `minor`. The package that carries the key is `@objectstack/spec`. `@objectstack/service-settings` may stay `patch` (the axis asks for one package at `minor` or above). `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right and agrees with `added`.

Whether a served-only payload belongs in the authorable register at all is a fair question, and a separate card; it is not this PR's to settle by leaving the gate red.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No `ui/**`, no `translations/**`, no second env detection in this repo (ruling 1 held: nothing here reads the AI env vars; the value comes only through the seam).
- No new route, no new permission; the gate is the page's own `readPermission`.
- New public names are the four the seat ruled: `SettingsLiveStatus.values`, `SettingsLiveValue` (exported from the package index), `SettingsService.liveStatementOf`, served `live`. `liveStatusOf` keeps its signature and delegates.
- Cross-repo: the service-ai half is carried in the PR body, not built here. Until it lands `live` is absent and the console reads "unknown", as ruled.
- Other check-runs on the head were still in progress at the time of reading (Test Core, Type Check, Lint families, Build); only `Check Changeset` had failed. This record does not vouch for the ones still running.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/system/settings-manifest.zod.ts` — holds against the ruling and its first consumer (#32021's checklist step reads `live.provider.source`). Optional, inline, closed `source` enum, `value` nullable string; absent = not stated is said in both the jsdoc and the `.describe`. Non-strict like its siblings, so an older reader strips it. No finding on the schema itself.

`settings-service.ts` (`liveStatementOf`, `servedLiveValues`, `liveValueMiss`) — agrees with the contract. Findings:

- **must-fix (M1, ②):** the declaration and level. In the PR body and in `.changeset/32052-settings-live-values.md` change `Metadata-protocol: none` to `Metadata-protocol: added`, and grade `'@objectstack/spec'` `minor` in the changeset front matter (`'@objectstack/service-settings'` may stay `patch`). Do not touch `authorable-surface/system.json` or its base. `Check Changeset` must be green on the new head.
- **should-fix (S1), not blocking:** "the key must be a declared option-bearing key" is enforced by type only on the declared branch (`optionTables` is filled for `select` / `radio` / `multiselect` alone). On the sourced branch `liveValueMiss` accepts any declared key that has a registered option source, without reading the specifier's type, and admission is then the source's own `admits`. `registerOptionSource` does not check the type either. The only source in the repo is `localization.locale` (a select), so nothing reachable today serves a non-option key; a later source registered on a text or password key would. Read the type in `liveValueMiss` (or record option-bearing keys at registration) and pin it. A follow-up card is enough.
- **nit (N1):** `liveValueMiss` reads `value` / `source` off the entry and `servedLiveValues` reads them a second time to build the served pair. An accessor-backed entry could answer differently on the second read. Return the validated pair from the check and serve that.
- **nit (N2):** for a sourced key the admission is `admits`, which by its own contract may hold for a second spelling of an offered option, so "always one of the page's own options" in the jsdoc, the changeset and the spec comment is slightly stronger than the code for sourced keys.
- **nit (N3):** the warn names the provider-supplied key of an undeclared entry. The ruling bars the value only, and the key name is what makes the line usable; noted because it is the one provider-controlled string in that log line.
- **nit (N4):** `servedLiveValues` runs outside the provider `try`, so a `values` object whose accessor throws becomes a 500 on the page read and not the error banner. In-process providers return plain objects; no pin needed.

`settings-routes.ts` — agrees: gate first, one provider call, `live` spread only when set. No finding.

`settings-routes.live-status.pin.test.ts`, `settings-manifest.test.ts` — cover each ruling as listed under ①. No finding.

`.changeset/32052-settings-live-values.md` — prose accurate; the declaration line and the spec level are M1.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-uunvxl`
Reviewed-by: `session_01ADHkmQKZzp4DLtqiCkZZRM`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

Must-fix, exact:

1. PR body: `Metadata-protocol: none` → `Metadata-protocol: added` (keep `Clause-②: yes (widening)`).
2. `.changeset/32052-settings-live-values.md`: body line `Metadata-protocol: none` → `Metadata-protocol: added`; front matter `'@objectstack/spec': patch` → `'@objectstack/spec': minor`. `'@objectstack/service-settings': patch` may stay.
3. `Check Changeset` green on the resulting head; no edit to `packages/spec/authorable-surface/**`.

The code, the schema, the pins, the census and the cloud carry all pass as they stand; a re-review of the new head needs to read only the changeset, the PR body and that check.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0190f5a236613dd7e360e0fc25b92339745bdfbf`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/settings-manifest.zod.ts + packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.types.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-routes.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-routes.live-status.pin.test.ts, packages/spec/src/system/settings-manifest.test.ts, packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json, content/docs/references/system/settings-manifest.mdx, docs/audits/2026-07-unknown-key-strictness-ledger.counts/system.md, .changeset/32052-settings-live-values.md

Round 2. Round 1 reviewed `047e94d6` in full and failed it on one must-fix (M1, the changeset declaration and level). This round read the one commit on top of it (`0190f5a2`, 3 files, +50/-31), the PR body's declaration lines, and the new head's check-runs; the round-1 findings on the unchanged files stand as written there. Nothing built or run locally.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The round's diff is what the dev declared, and nothing else.** Three files: the changeset (two lines), `settings-service.ts` (`liveStatementOf` and the entry judge), and one new pin in `settings-routes.live-status.pin.test.ts`. No edit under `packages/spec/**`, so the schema, its test, `authorable-surface/system.json`, the reference page and the strictness count are byte-identical to the head round 1 read. The route file is untouched.
- **Served answers that existed before: still unchanged.** No provider returns `{}` before the `try`. A banner-only statement has `values` undefined, skips the new block and builds the same six-field banner. A provider throw takes the same arm with the same warn and error banner; `live = undefined` there is the only addition. A falsy status still returns `{}`.
- **Gate order: unchanged.** The route was not touched: `getNamespace` (the 403) first, then the single `liveStatementOf` call.
- **N4 (values read inside the provider guard): done, no new leak path.** The `values` read and `servedLiveValues` now sit inside the provider `try`; a throw there takes the existing throw arm, which resets `live`, so a half-judged record cannot be served beside the error banner. The dropped-entries warn is the same text as before (key name plus fixed reason, never the value). New pin: a statement whose `values` accessor throws answers 200, the error banner, no `live`, one warn.
- **N1 (entry read once): done.** `judgeLiveValue` destructures `value` and `source` from the entry once and returns the pair it judged (`{ value: null, source }` for `none`, the checked string otherwise); `servedLiveValues` serves that pair and never reads the entry again. Same checks in the same order as `liveValueMiss`, same reason strings.
- **Pins:** the round-1 set is unchanged and still covers each ruling; one pin added for N4.

### ② Semver level

**M1 fixed.** `.changeset/32052-settings-live-values.md` at this head: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, `'@objectstack/service-settings': patch`, body line `Metadata-protocol: added` beside `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. The PR body carries the same two lines. `added` is the kind the moved shard records (the row `system/SettingsNamespacePayload:live`), and ruling A on #25105 then puts the package that carries it at `minor`; `patch` for service-settings is right, since nothing an author writes moved there.

`Check Changeset` on this head: two runs. The first (job 129640908406) is red because it read the PR body before the edit (its log quotes `Metadata-protocol: none`). The newest (job 129642083258, started after the body edit) is **success**. The newest governs.

This amends the step-0 ruling of `none` / `patch` to `added` / spec `minor`. Whether a served-only payload should be in the authorable register at all remains a question for a separate card.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Unchanged from round 1: no `ui/**`, no `translations/**`, no second env detection, no new route or permission, the four ruled public names only, the service-ai half carried in the PR body.
- Check-runs still in progress at the time of reading: Test Core 1-8, the four Type Check jobs, six Lint jobs, Build Core / Docs / UI Deps, Live E2E UI, and a second PR-body guards run. None had failed; this record does not vouch for them.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/system/settings-manifest.zod.ts` — unchanged this round; holds as judged in round 1. No finding.

`settings-service.ts` — agrees with the contract. Remaining findings, none blocking:

- **should-fix (S1, open from round 1, follow-up card):** the option-bearing type is enforced only on the declared branch; a declared key of any type with a registered option source is servable, admission then being the source's `admits`. Only `localization.locale` (a select) has a source today, so nothing reachable serves a non-option key.
- **nit (N5, new with N4):** with the judging inside the guard, anything thrown while judging (a source's `admits` that throws, say) now lands in the pre-existing throw warn, which prints `err.message`. That text is authored by the provider or the option source, not by this code, and before this round the same throw was a 500 through the route's fault path; noted so the next option source does not put the value in its error text. It also means such a throw replaces the stated banner with the error banner, which is the throw rule, not the invalid-entry rule.
- **nit (N2, N3, open):** "always one of the page's own options" is slightly stronger than `admits` for a sourced key; the warn names the provider-supplied key of an undeclared entry (the ruling bars the value only).

`settings-routes.live-status.pin.test.ts` — the new pin asserts what N4 claims. No finding.

`.changeset/32052-settings-live-values.md` — declaration and levels correct; prose unchanged and accurate.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-uunvxl`
Reviewed-by: `session_01ADHkmQKZzp4DLtqiCkZZRM`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## ACCEPT — #32052 at `0190f5a236613dd7e360e0fc25b92339745bdfbf`

**维护者速读**：`GET /api/settings/:namespace` 新增可选字段 `live`，由运行时通过已有的 live-status 接缝声明某个键「实际生效」的值和来源（`settings` / `environment` / `none`）。控制台的首次使用清单据此判断内置 AI 是否已配好（#32021）。读权限先校验，再询问提供方。只复制「值 + 来源」，值必须是该键选项表里允许的选项，不会带出任何密钥。没有提供方时不返回 `live`，表示「未知」，与运行时明确声明的「无」区分开。本仓库单独运行时没有提供方，现有返回逐字节不变。由 cloud 的 service-ai 来填 `values.provider`，已写在 PR 正文的 "Carried to repo:cloud" 一节。

Seat check:
- Contract review (schema face, `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`):
  - Round 1: FAIL 6759409809. M1 was the seat's own step-0 error: the authorable-surface row moved, so the line is `Metadata-protocol: added` and spec takes a minor bump.
  - Round 2: **PASS** 6759520565. M1 is fixed. N4 (a throwing `values` accessor now gives the error banner, not a 500) and N1 are folded in and pinned.
- Open, non-blocking: S1 (the option-bearing type is not checked for a key with a registered option source; `localization.locale` is the only such key today) and nits N2, N3 and N5.
- CI at the head: 72 check-runs, none pending. The one red row is the stale `Check Changeset` run 129640908406, which read the PR body before it was patched. The newer run 129642083258 is green and governs.
- Governed: 0 of 14 paths are governed, and the PR is under the human-merge threshold.
- Thread runs: service-settings 1456/1456 plus routes 199/199 at the head, typecheck and lint pass, gates 116/116, and ablations A1–A6 go red as expected and are restored.
- Changesets: `@objectstack/spec` minor and `@objectstack/service-settings` patch, with `Metadata-protocol: added` and `Clause-②: yes (widening)`.

Landing: ready + auto-merge.
